events.description: Second of the roundtables between the five Eastern Caribbean CBI states and the US Treasury on implementing the Six CBI Principles.
events.quote: the second was held in Miami in October 2023

events.title: Third US-Caribbean Roundtable on CBI (Grenada): four of six principles fully implemented
events.description: The five Eastern Caribbean CBI states (Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, St Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia) and the US Treasury met in Grenada. All five were reported to have fully implemented Principles 1 (treatment of denials), 2 (interviews), 3 (FIU checks) and 6 (suspension of applications from Russians and Belarusians); audits and retrieval of revoked passports were still being implemented. The March 2024 MOA was signed by all five, and an Interim Regulatory Commission was to be appointed to set up the regional regulator.
events.quote: On 29 August 2024, the five Eastern Caribbean countries 1 that offer Citizenship by Investment (CBI) Programmes and the United States Department of the Treasury held a productive Roundtable in Grenada

events.title: US INCSR 2003: Dominica, St Kitts and Nevis and Nauru sell economic citizenship; sales called a law-enforcement impediment
events.description: In the State Department's Offshore Financial Services Table for 2003 (issued March 2004), Dominica, St. Kitts & Nevis and Nauru are marked Y under 'Sells Economic Citizenship'; the other listed centres are N or blank. The narrative warns that improperly controlled sales of economic citizenship let buyers obtain a passport in a new name.

events.title: PRA board rebrands the SRRV into SMILE, Classic, Courtesy and Human Touch options

The report dates the decision 20 October 2010 on p. 10 and 22 October 2010 (245th board meeting) on p. 78.
events.quote: On October 20, 2010, the PRA Board rationalized, expanded and branded PRA’s retirement visa product-line

events.title: Development Bank of the Philippines made depository bank for SRRV visa deposits

events.title: Harmonisation of old and new SRRV deposit schemes (1.5% fee on released excess deposits)

events.title: SRRV options (SMILE, Classic, Human Touch, Courtesy) launched
events.description: PRA introduced and launched the SRRV options for foreign retirees and former Filipinos on 5 May 2011, after the board decision of October 2010.
events.quote: *05 May 2011, PRA introduced and launched various SRRV Options for foreign retirees and former Filipino citizens

events.title: SRRV applications and processing suspended during COVID-19; enrolment falls 71.6%
events.description: With travel bans and the suspension of SRRV application and processing in 2020, PRA reported a 71.6% fall in 2020 enrolment compared with 2019. The report gives no dates for the suspension.

events.quote: with the imposition of travel bans as well as suspension of SRRV application and processing, we registered a 71.6% decrease in our 2020 enrolment compared to 2019.

new_indicators.name: Irregular investor residence grants detected
new_indicators.definition: Persons found by an auditor, prosecutor or other authority to have obtained investor-linked residence irregularly (e.g. by a sham change of status to company partner), in or up to the stated period, whether or not the residence was withdrawn.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-other for the Oman State Audit Institution finding (2024 Society Summary, p. 40). Residence counterpart of irregular_naturalisations_detected.

new_indicators.name: Net enrolment in an investor residence programme
new_indicators.definition: New programme residents admitted in a period (gross enrolment) minus memberships or permits cancelled in the same period, as printed by the source. A flow, not the stock of holders.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-other for the Philippine SRRV, whose reports print gross enrolment, cancellations and net enrolment by year.

new_indicators.name: Programme deposits returned on exit
new_indicators.definition: Refundable programme deposits (e.g. SRRV visa deposits) paid back to members who left the programme or died, in a period.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-other (Philippine Retirement Authority visa-deposit tables). Companion to rbi_investment_total (gross deposits brought in).

new_indicators.name: Net programme deposits
new_indicators.definition: Refundable programme deposits brought in by new members minus deposits returned to leaving members, in a period, as printed by the source.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-other. The PRA calls it net foreign currency generated from visa deposits. Note: an existing row from phl-pra-ar-2017 records a net figure under rbi_investment_total.

new_indicators.name: Programme deposits held (stock)
new_indicators.definition: Refundable deposits of programme members held by the agency or its depository banks at a date.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-other (PRA restricted visa deposits / trust liabilities).

new_indicators.name: Net income of the programme agency
new_indicators.definition: Net income of the agency running the programme in a period. Use breakdown category= for the measure the source prints: net_operating_income, net_income_before_tax, net_income_after_tax.

ledger.contains: UAE federal portal page on the Golden visa (updated 28 Jul 2026): benefits list, and a table of eligible categories with residence duration and main requirements (investors, entrepreneurs, exceptional talents, outstanding students, humanitarian pioneers). Only the investor row is in scope: minimum capital AED 2 million (already a term) and the alternative of contributing to an establishment paying at least AED 250,000 a year in taxes (added). No statistics.

WAM report of the UAE Cabinet session of 20 May 2018: adoption of a long-term entry/residence visa system for investors and talents (up to 10 years; 5 years for students, 10 for exceptional students) and the aim of 100% foreign ownership by year end (already an event). The rest of the article covers unrelated Cabinet decisions (sign-language dictionary, Hajj rules, school calendar, embassies). No statistics and no minimum amounts.

One-page written answer (Senate Supplementary Budget Estimates, 19 Nov 2013, SE13/0222): Significant Investor visa applications lodged (545) and approved (75) between 24 Nov 2012 and 30 Nov 2013, and a statement that no estimates were made at launch. Both numbers were already extracted; nothing else in scope.

Two-page FOI release (request of 14 June 2016). p. 1: lodgements and grants of primary applications for BIIP subclass 188 (Business Innovation, Investor, Significant Investor, Premium Investor streams) and subclass 888 (same streams) by programme year 2012-13 to 2015-16 (to 31 May 2016); Premium Investor and most 888 cells are N/A; top-five citizenship countries per stream (ranking only, no counts); notes on the 1992 start of Business Skills, SIV start 24 Nov 2012 and PIV start 1 Jul 2015. p. 2: Business Talent (subclass 132) primary lodgements and grants by programme year 2008-09 to 2015-16 (to 31 May 2016), and its top-five source countries (ranking only). All printed counts extracted; N/A cells and country rankings have no numbers. No totals printed, so nothing to add up.

Whole issue of La Gaceta No. 135 (14 Jul 2021, 80 pp.). In scope only pp. 2-3: Ley 9996 (attraction of investors, rentistas and pensioners): tax and import incentives (one-time duty-free household goods, up to two vehicles duty-free, income-tax exemption on the declared qualifying income, 20% exemption from property transfer tax, duty-free professional equipment), no automatic tax residence, new investor minimum of US$150,000 (already a term), special DGME service window, 10% fine for forged documents, regulations within 60 days, benefits available for the first five years and kept for ten (already events); approved by the Assembly on 22 Jun 2021 (event added), signed 5 Jul 2021, in force on publication. The rest of the issue (ministerial leave orders, civil aviation, trademarks, individual naturalisation notices, tenders, municipal notices) is unrelated. No statistics.

Five-page government table summarising the clauses of the Immigration (Transition) (Amendment and Validation) Act 2025 (items 1-33; items 9 and 28 are not printed). Mostly work permits, Caymanian status, RERC, caregivers, farmhands, term limits and marriages of convenience (out of scope). In scope: item 10 (holders of a Certificate of Direct Investment and of a Residency Certificate (Substantial Business Presence) must file annual declarations), items 18-19 (permanent residence for persons of independent means: investment in developed real estate whose paid-up value meets the prescribed sum at the time of application; certificate held 10 years, re-applying at year 9, before naturalisation), and new definitions of 'developed real estate' and 'paid-up amount'. No amounts for the programmes (only 'prescribed sum'), no dates and no statistics. These rule changes are already in the timeline as event e-809a44287d, taken from the Act itself (cym-imm-trans-amend-act-2025, in force 1 May 2026), so no duplicate events were added; this summary gives no commencement date of its own.

ECCB/OECS news release of 5 Sep 2024 on the third US-Caribbean Roundtable on CBI (Grenada, 29 Aug 2024): the five Eastern Caribbean CBI states and the US Treasury reviewed the Six CBI Principles (agreed Feb 2023, already an event); four principles (denials, interviews, FIU checks, suspension of Russian and Belarusian applicants) reported fully implemented, audits and retrieval of revoked passports still in progress; earlier roundtables in St Kitts (Feb 2023) and Miami (Oct 2023); March 2024 MOA now signed by all five; an Interim Regulatory Commission to be appointed. Events added for the Miami and Grenada roundtables. No numbers.

US State Department INCSR 2002 (issued March 2003) Offshore Financial Services Table: for about 60 offshore centres, counts of offshore banks and IBCs, Y/N for trusts, bearer shares, asset protection trusts, insurance, 'Sells Economic Citizenship', internet gaming, money-laundering law, FATF NCCT status and memberships; footnotes on abbreviations. Only the 'Sells Economic Citizenship' column is in scope (no numbers): Y for Dominica, St. Kitts & Nevis and Nauru, N for every other listed jurisdiction including Antigua and Barbuda, Grenada, Belize, St. Lucia and St. Vincent; Guatemala, Botswana, Brunei and Andorra blank. Event added for the Y list (the Belize N was already an event). Bank and company counts are about offshore finance, out of scope.

US State Department INCSR 2003 Vol. II (March 2004) chapter on offshore financial centres: narrative on FATF NCCT progress, shell banks, IBCs, internet gaming; one sentence calling the sale of 'economic citizenship' (passports sold to foreigners who promise to invest), if improperly controlled, an impediment to law enforcement, since buyers can obtain a passport in a new name; explanatory notes defining the table columns (Y = sells economic citizenship); Offshore Financial Services Table for 2003. In scope only the 'Sells Economic Citizenship' column (no numbers): Y for Dominica, St. Kitts & Nevis and Nauru, N for the other listed centres (Grenada, Antigua and Barbuda, Belize, St. Lucia, St. Vincent and others), blank for Guatemala, Botswana, Brunei, Andorra. Event added (Nauru Y was already an event). Bank/IBC counts and the '30 OFCs' with internet gambling are out of scope.

INIS press release of 5 July 2013: Minister announces changes to the Immigrant Investor Programme after its first-year review, effective 15 July 2013 (already an event); 9 applications approved to date with project investment of over EUR 10m (already extracted) and predicted employment of over 123 jobs (added as a projection); list of changes and a note-for-editors table comparing current and revised minimums for bond, enterprise, fund, mixed and endowment options (revised terms already in program_terms; current terms are in program_terms from the 2012 guidelines); tuition fees reckonable; Evaluation Committee membership.

Official record of all Dáil written answers of 4 May 2022 (Akoma Ntoso XML). In scope only two answers by the Minister for Justice on the Immigrant Investor Programme: Q391 (more than 1,400 applications approved, investment over EUR 1 billion; added) and Q405-408 (legal basis: Government Decision April 2012; Stamp 4 permission; evaluation committee; renewals at years two and five; 2019 audit and EY review, already events; table of applications received, approved and value of approved investment by year 2012-2021 with totals; table of approvals and value by investment type, cumulative to end 2021; all added). Every other answer of the day is unrelated. Check: yearly rows add up to the totals (2,249; 1,431; 1,052,550,000); approvals by type add up to 1,431, but values by type add up to 1,053,550,000, EUR 1m more than the printed total.

MOTAC MM2H 'Category Overview' web page (last update 10 Feb 2026): one table of requirements for Platinum, Gold, Silver and SEZ/SFZ (age 50+ and 21-49) categories: fixed deposit, term (20/15/5/10/10 years), minimum age, compulsory home purchase, participating fee, processing fee, minimum days per year, deposit withdrawal (max 50%), dependants (children up to 34), tax exemption, renewal fee. All amounts added as program_terms with this source (they repeat the categories page already in the data). SEZ/SFZ property price is 'as set for SEZ property development' (no number). The page's visitor counters are not about the programme. No statistics.

Immigration New Zealand announcement of 9 Sep 2026: eligible Build to Rent developments become an acceptable Growth-category investment for the Active Investor Plus visa in December 2026, via approved managed funds meeting capability, governance and delivery requirements; details to follow (already an event). No amounts and no statistics; the rest of the page is site navigation.

Public 'Society Summary' (92 pp., Arabic) of Oman's State Financial and Administrative Audit Institution 2024 annual report: audit findings and corrective actions across ministries and state companies (finance, tax, housing, health, education, labour, Muscat municipality, commerce, transport, energy, OQ, food and poultry companies, etc.). In scope only: p. 40 (Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion, audit of the Invest Easy services centre 2022-2023): 378 workers in low-skill occupations obtained investor residence after changing their residence permit to 'commercial partner' (added as a number; already an event), and foreign investors using the exemption from the OMR 3,000 three-yearly commercial-register fee to obtain residence without real investment capacity; p. 31 (Labour, Dhofar 2022): work-licence applications for 'commercial partner, chairman, CEO' of people meeting the 5- or 10-year investor residence programme conditions were suspended pending checks on the investor's seriousness (undated corrective action, so no event); p. 41: 52 investors left the commercial register without their foreign-investor incentives being withdrawn (incentives, not residence; not added). Everything else is out of scope.

MICI press release of 3 Jul 2023 on the minister's four-year record: exports, export programmes, trade intelligence, safeguards, investment regimes (SEM headquarters licences, EMMA, free zones), Qualified Investor Programme, film production, industry, Minera Panamá contract. In scope only the Qualified Investor sentence: 207 qualified investors who have invested B/. 115.6 million, mainly in real estate, banking and securities (both already extracted). The SEM, EMMA and free-zone figures are business-licence regimes, not investment migration; everything else is unrelated.

PRA Annual Report 2016 (108 pp.). In scope and extracted: key figures (p. 5, image, OCR: rounded repeats of figures below); GM message (2016 dividend, 2017 commitment of 10,000 retirees); 2016 scorecard targets (pp. 30-31) and accomplishments with 2012-2016 series (pp. 44-47: net visa deposits, retention rate, net enrolment, principals enrolled by marketers, revenue, net operating income); SRRV highlights (p. 49 nationality counts and shares and net enrolment chart, repeats of Appendix B; p. 50 region chart and FX chart, repeats); financial highlights (p. 51: dividends, revenue and net income before tax 2014-2016); COA audit report and statements (pp. 68-84: revenue, fee lines, net income, dividends, restricted visa deposits US$207.6m, 2016 applicants 2,744/2,044, new enrolees with deposits 4,834, fee and deposit rules, DBP agreement 2011, product line 2010); Appendix A scorecard (pp. 86-96, scanned, OCR: 2015 targets); Appendix B statistics (p. 97 yearly enrolment and cancellation by principal/dependant 1987-2016; p. 98 cumulative enrolment by top-10 nationality and active retirees by region; p. 99 monthly gross deposits, withdrawals and net deposits 1987-2016). Out of scope: organisation, board, strategy, marketing and training activities, risk, governance, CSR, ISO, customer-satisfaction and marketing-plan KPIs, walk-in growth rates, after-enrolment service counts (p. 52, p. 100), accreditation counts (marketers 153/168, merchants 5/14, facilities 45/67), PRA operating budget, expenses, taxes, PPE and treasury investments. Checks: all Appendix B tables add up (see notes); 2016 fee lines add to PHP 72 more than the printed total; 2015 net enrolment is 4,155 on p. 45 but 4,144 on pp. 49 and 97; 2015 net deposits US$36,323,000 on p. 44 but US$36,135,000 on pp. 50 and 99; revenue 2014-2015 differs between p. 46 and the p. 51 chart; active retirees 36,302 (p. 98) vs 36,343 memberships (pp. 78, 97); 2016 dividend 'remitted' is PHP 210.4m on p. 51 but PHP 190.441m on p. 69 (timing).
ledger.to_do: Appendix A scorecard (PDF pp. 91-92, scanned): the 2015 targets for net enrolment and net operating income are illegible in OCR and were not recorded; also its 2012-2014 baselines (e.g. retention 96.00% for 2014 vs 96.51% on p. 45) were not recorded. Not recorded for lack of a fitting indicator: 8,326 members who paid the annual PRA fee in 2016 (p. 83); visitorial fees receivable of PHP 36.9m of which PHP 26.4m provided for as uncollectable because members' whereabouts are unknown (pp. 70, 80); interest on visa deposits (US$392,048.41 reinvested, US$1.124m unclaimed by members; pp. 81-82).

ledger.contains: PRA Annual Report 2019 (73 pp., no financial statements: the audited report is posted separately). In scope and extracted: GM message (2019 dividends PHP 216.4m; 53,265 gross enrolled; revenue target exceeded by 9.22% / PHP 85.7m, a printed difference not recorded as a level); Financial Highlights charts (p. 6: NOI, dividends and foreign currency generated 2018-2019 and cumulative); Enrollment Highlights (p. 7: cumulative enrolled 60,359 / 68,383, gross enrolment bars 2014-2019; 2018-2019 were already extracted; percentage changes 21.70% / 10.81% / 23.74% are derived and not recorded); SRRV options and deposits (pp. 13-14; two terms already extracted, four added; 5 May 2011 launch); 2019 scorecard (pp. 49-52: outstanding visa deposits US$548.4m, cumulative net enrolment 49,271, revenue, NOI, with targets). Out of scope: organisation, marketing events and ads, merchant-partner and facility usage counts, accreditation counts (267 marketers, 20 merchants, 43 facilities), 3,405 marketing leads, satisfaction survey (88%/56%), budget utilisation, return on marketing expense, ISO, governance, FOI requests, staff directory. The report is internally inconsistent (cumulative enrolment 68,383 vs 53,265; 2019 NOI 281.4m vs 432,746 thousand; 2019 dividend 216.4m vs 258,489 thousand; revenue target exceeded vs revenue at 48% of target); all printed versions were recorded with notes. Chart scales (p. 6) are not printed and were read as thousands (see notes).

PRA Annual Report 2020 (64 pp., no financial statements). In scope and extracted: GM message (71.6% fall in enrolment, suspension of SRRV applications, P150M remitted for CY 2020, over US$572m deposits, net operating revenue over PHP 454m); Financial Highlights charts (p. 5: NOI 2019-2020 and cumulative, dividends 2019 and '-' for 2020, foreign currency generated 2019-2020 and cumulative); enrolled retirees 55,114 at end-2020 (already extracted) and average net enrolment 2017-2020; SRRV schemes (pp. 11-12; Expanded Courtesy terms added; SMILE/Classic/Human Touch/Courtesy deposits are the same as in the 2019 report already recorded); 2020 scorecard (pp. 41-44: outstanding deposits US$572.9m, cumulative net enrolment target, NOI, with targets). The GM's 'net operating revenue of more than PhP 454 Million' is recorded as revenue with a note (undefined, differs from the NOI on p. 42). Percentage changes are derived and not recorded. Out of scope: satisfaction survey, marketing leads (613), events and ads, accreditation counts (24 merchant partners, 96 facilities, 151 marketers), ID renewals (19,629 in 2020; 20,583 in 2019), social-integration activities, merchant/facility usage, processing-time, ISO, IT, competency measures, governance, FOI, organisation. Chart scales are not printed (see notes).

EDB media release of 2 Mar 2023 (5 pp.): changes to GIP Options A, B and C effective 15 Mar 2023 (new minimums already in program_terms; event already recorded), hiring conditions for re-entry permit renewal, 24,699 jobs created by GIP investors 2011-2022 and an average of 60 investors granted PR a year in 2020-2022 (both already extracted), March 2020 revision (already an event), GIP introduced in 2004 (already an event), and an annex comparing existing and new requirements. Added: the pre-15-March-2023 minimums printed in the annex (S$2.5m for Options A, B and C; family-office AUM S$200m with S$50m held in Singapore; S$2m total business expenditure by year 5) and the new S$50m AUM maintenance condition. Hiring counts (employees to be hired) are conditions without money amounts and are given in notes.

Singapore Parliament written answer of 5 Aug 2026 (Gan Kim Yong for the PM): more than 2,000 single family offices received 13O/13U tax incentives at end-December 2025 (already extracted), families mainly from Asia Pacific then Europe and the Americas (no numbers), and Singapore's asset management industry grew 10.1% in 2025 to $6.7 trillion AUM (whole industry, out of scope). The question asked for AUM by country and pending applications, but the answer gives no such figures.

One-page Thailand Privilege Card package table: Gold, Platinum, Diamond and Reserve (validity 5/10/15/20+ years, primary fees THB 900,000 / 1.5m / 2.5m / 5m, supplementary fees THB 1m / 1.5m / 2m, privilege points, transfer and upgrade rules, privileges), Bronze (5 years, THB 650,000) and the Thailand Privilege Pass (Lite THB 9,900, Lifestyle 150,000, Beyond 250,000, Corporate 500,000; one-year lifestyle memberships). All card fees are already in program_terms. The Privilege Pass is not recorded: the table presents it as a one-year lifestyle membership and nothing in the document links it to a visa. Points, privileges and validity periods are not amounts. No statistics.

NIA guidelines (6 pp., English) for the Alien Permanent Resident Certificate (Plum Blossom Card) for special contributors, senior professionals and investment immigrants: legal basis, eligible groups, investor routes (business investment over NTD 15 million creating jobs for 5+ nationals for 3 years; central government bonds over NTD 30 million held 3 years; both already in program_terms), required documents, application channels, fee of NTD 10,000 per item with special contributors and senior professionals exempt (added as a term for investors), exemption from the 183-day residence rule at application, and revocation if average residence over five years is under 183 days. No dates of change and no statistics.

Citizenship Investment Act 2015 (Samoa), revised to 31 Dec 2022 (15 pp.): definitions; any nationality eligible (Minister may exclude countries); qualifying investments listed in the Schedule; eligibility: invest at least WST 4m within 3 years (already a term) and net worth of at least WST 2.5m (added); option of developing a lease of government land; application documents and due diligence; refusal grounds; at least 70% (or a prescribed share of at least 50%) of the investment sum to be placed in a Samoan fixed deposit before formal approval, 15% to be kept during residence; 3-year permanent resident permit; citizenship after 3 years with 15 days' residence a year; passports valid 5 years; investment kept 5 years, or reinvested at least WST 1m (added); cancellation grounds; licensing of promoters and agents (fines up to 50 penalty units or 2 years); annual report to Parliament by 30 June; Minister may raise amounts; regulations may set fees and a quota. Assent 5 Nov 2015 and commencement 31 Jan 2017 already events. No statistics.

Two-page Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour brochure (Dec 2024) on Samoa citizenship by investment: background, qualifying investment areas, minimum investment SAT 4 million (already a term) and minimum net worth SAT 2.5 million, application contents, the three steps (temporary permit, 3-year permanent permit with 15% of the deposit kept, citizenship after 15 days' residence a year), and a fee table (application and due-diligence fees by family member, promoter and agent application fees). All amounts added as program_terms. No statistics.
